system:
Resolve reference/request licences for each visual attribute. Return only governs and reasons matching the supplied JSON contract. Interpret the complete request semantically, without keyword lists. The separate medium_decision already settles rendering-medium permission and taxonomy: the medium owner is pinned by the schema. Host code computes the style phrase, transformation phrase/target, discrepancy and note from the accepted medium decision. Do not return those host-owned fields.
With no visual reference, every visual attribute is request-governed. Otherwise the reference governs every attribute the user has not actually specified. Explicit requests outrank observed references, and references outrank director notes. A director only fills unresolved space. Source metadata, target aspect, duration and creativity are not instructions about camera framing, lighting, wardrobe, palette or rendering process. A stale Asset.Description is caller commentary; actual Card observations govern reference appearance. Independent reference_readings are real supplied readings even when this analysis attaches no conditioning media.
Action: a requested new action or performed behavior overrides a subject plate's static pose, including an explicit vocal performance or speaking action. Action authority concerns what the figure is asked to do, not only locomotion; a performance request does not need physical travel. An intelligible requested behavior remains an action when the caller uses imperfect tense, inflection or grammar; do not claim no action merely because the sentence is ungrammatical. Merely changing which figure performs an existing source action does not itself change that action. Wardrobe: a requested clothing/accessory change overrides only the named properties; otherwise retain the corresponding figure's observed clothes. Framing: an actual requested camera composition, shot scale, viewpoint or movement governs; merely being somewhere, moving in a direction or choosing a canvas ratio does not. Lighting: an instruction about the light, an illuminating source, its direction or its visible quality governs. Placement under an illuminating practical source therefore governs that light; weather, time of day, location, an object whose name implies a time, and mood alone do not authorize replacing reference lighting. Palette includes the scene's color and tonal grading, saturation and contrast treatment. An explicit requested grade/tonal contrast therefore governs palette even without a new hue. An object's incidental color does not recolor or regrade the scene.
In an edit, the edit_source clip owns the scene's observed appearance before incoming identity portraits. Incoming replacement/placement images supply identity; their studio lighting/backdrop must not replace the clip's world. For a non-frame content reference, sheet panels, labels, multiple views and posing are presentation, not the new scene or identity. For actual_frame sources, the entire supplied image is the target frame at its anchored instant: preserve those pixels, including their complete layout and source background. Never authorize sheet cleanup on an actual frame merely because it is a sheet. An observed pose is licensed only for an actual frame anchor, never as an identity attribute. Keep rendering restyling independent of retention relationship: changing a medium does not itself select attribute_transfer.
Target identities are already resolved by identity_requirements. Those are TARGET descriptors and properties after explicit caller requirements; original observed_subjects remain the SOURCE. Do not reassert a conflicting source gender/species/age/wardrobe as a request error. Neither re-author those identity decisions nor return identity fields. Resolve only the remaining attribute owners and their reasons.

brief.intent: the woman in the technical jacket rides the dragon into an epic battleground, cinematic hollywood scene with dramatic expressions and camera movements

cards.summary: Cinematic character reference sheet presenting one tactical-dressed figure in a rainy nighttime hero scene, three full-body studio views, and four detail close-ups.

subjects.descriptor: Adult with East Asian features and a medium build, shown across multiple views of the same character reference sheet.
attributes: adult, East Asian features, medium build
short dark hair with shaved sides and a small tied knot or bun at the back
small scar through one eyebrow
black stand-collar tactical jacket with chest strap and metal buckle
black T-shirt
black cargo trousers
black lace-up combat boots
pose: standing upright with arms relaxed at the sides in the hero, front, and back views
turned in profile in the side view
neutral, serious expression in the portrait close-up

cards.environment: Top panel: a rain-slicked urban bridge or walkway at night with metal railings and warm streetlights in the background. Lower panels: a dark charcoal studio backdrop.
cards.lighting: Low-key cinematic lighting; cool blue-gray rainy night with warm amber lamp highlights in the hero panel, and soft directional studio lighting in the reference panels.
cards.framing: Vertical composite reference sheet: a large environmental full-body shot at the top, three full-body turnaround views in the middle row, and four detail close-ups in the bottom row.
cards.style: Photorealistic cinematic character concept art and reference sheet, high contrast, gritty, rain-soaked atmosphere.
cards.characterisation: A stoic, combat-ready figure in an all-black tactical outfit, presented as a single character identity across the sheet.

cards.summary: A dark fantasy creature reference sheet for a single black-scaled dragon, combining one large atmospheric scene at the top with a front/side/rear turnaround row and four close-up detail panels (head, wing membrane, claw and foot, scale texture).

subjects.descriptor: Large winged dragon with dark iridescent scales and long swept-back horns
attributes: charcoal-black to blue-black armored scales with teal and blue iridescence
several long pale bone-colored horns swept back from the skull
row of tall spikes along neck, spine and tail
long tapering tail
large membranous wings with thin veined skin and dark finger struts
four legs with scaled feet and curved pale talons
small amber eye
pose: top panel: standing on all fours, head lowered, wings partly raised
FRONT panel: facing viewer, wings spread symmetrically
SIDE PROFILE panel: standing in profile, tail extended
REAR panel: viewed from behind, wings spread
detail panels: head, wing, foot and scales shown close-up

cards.environment: Top panel: dark volcanic terrain with jagged rock formations, wet reflective black ground and distant orange lava glow under heavy dark haze; remaining panels: plain dark gradient studio backdrop.
cards.lighting: Moody low-key lighting overall; top panel lit by dim diffuse sky light with warm orange lava glow from the background, turnaround and detail panels lit by soft top-down studio-style light with specular highlights on scales and horns.
cards.framing: Single wide landscape sheet divided into panels: a full-width scene at top, a row of three equal full-body views, and a row of four equal close-up crops.
cards.style: Dark fantasy photorealistic creature concept art / character design reference sheet
cards.characterisation: Menacing, ancient, armored dragon design emphasizing heavy scales, horns and spikes.

rendering_permission.reasoning: The request describes scene action and appends a descriptive style tag (“cinematic hollywood scene with dramatic expressions and camera movements”). It contains no authorizing rendering operation or grammatical instruction to transform or directly render the attached visual reference in a specified target style/medium.

medium_decision.retained_style: Photorealistic cinematic character concept art, high contrast, gritty, rain-soaked atmosphere
medium_decision.reasoning: The host rendering permission is preserve, so no rendering transformation is authorized. The request adds scene action plus cinematic/dramatic descriptors, but it names no target medium or rendering operation. The selected source is a content reference sheet, so retained_style copies the observed visual style while removing only reference-sheet packaging. The observed concept-art reference is classified as digitally drawn illustration; requested medium and requested style remain empty because the wording provides treatments/descriptors rather than a medium noun phrase.
